subject: Social Media
title: Community Notes and Crowdsourcing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Community Notes and Crowdsourcing.

hook.text: A politician posts a false claim. Within minutes, a Community Note appears below it with corrections and sources.

buildup.text: X's Community Notes lets users from different viewpoints rate context. Only notes approved across divides appear.

discovery.text: The system uses bridging algorithms. Notes that unite left and right get shown. Partisan notes get filtered out.

twist.text: Community Notes works better than expected. Even its critics admit the cross-partisan requirement reduces bias.

climax.text: But it's slow. False claims spread for hours before notes appear. And powerful users can discourage note writers.

punchline.text: Crowdsourced truth is messy. It's still better than none.

quiz.question: What makes Community Notes different from regular fact-checking?
options: Notes must be approved by people across political divides
